Perform statistical analysis on scores using a specified test

scores.stat.analysis.Rd

Unified interface for testing associations between any score matrix and a clinical/experimental trait. Accepts cell group scores, NMF latent factors (output of compute.latent_factors()), or any samples x features matrix.

Usage

scores.stat.analysis(
  scores,
  coldata,
  trait,
  test = c("fisher", "wilcox", "anova", "kruskal", "ttest"),
  pval = 0.05,
  padj = FALSE
)

Arguments

scores

A list, NMF output from compute.latent_factors(), or a score matrix (samples x features). When a list, the first element must be the score matrix; optional second and third elements (e.g. the output of construct_cell_groups()) are subsetted to the significant features and returned with their names.

coldata

A data frame (or tibble) containing clinical or experimental metadata for samples. Must include the column specified in trait. Its rows are matched to the samples of the scores by row name; without sample names, they must be in the order of the scores. Samples with a missing trait are left out.

trait

Character. The name of the column in coldata representing the clinical or experimental trait to test against (e.g., response, subtype, etc.). It must be categorical.

test

Character. Statistical test to perform. One of:

  • "fisher" - Fisher's exact test (scores binarised at median)

  • "wilcox" - Wilcoxon rank-sum test (non-parametric, binary traits)

  • "anova" - One-way ANOVA (parametric, two or more groups)

  • "kruskal" - Kruskal-Wallis test (non-parametric, two or more groups)

  • "ttest" - Welch's t-test (parametric, binary traits)

Only one can be used per call; defaults to the first one ("fisher").

pval

Numeric. Threshold for significance: a feature is significant if its (adjusted) p-value is <= pval (default: 0.05).

padj

Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple testing across the features with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, and the adjusted p-values are compared with the threshold. Default FALSE.

Value

A list whose first element is the score matrix restricted to the significant features (no column if none is significant). Optional second and third elements (from the input list, e.g. the composition and weights of the cell groups) are subsetted accordingly and keep their names. The last element, Statistics, is a data frame with the test of every feature (feature, test, statistic_name, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, significant).

Details

The function automatically calls the corresponding statistical test function based on the test argument:

  • scores.fisher.test()

  • scores.wilcox.test()

  • scores.anova.test()

  • scores.kruskal.test()

  • scores.ttest()

Each test produces both a statistical result and visual outputs (PDF plots) stored in the "Results/" folder for the significant features. These visualizations include the relevant test results (p-values) annotated on the plots.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
data("traitdata.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Dendrogram plots saved to: Results/Dendrogram_color_clusters.pdf
#> 44 of 897 features were not assigned to any cluster by the tree cut and are not part of any cell group (pink: 2, yellow: 8, red: 2, blue: 6, brown: 4, turquoise: 12, black: 4, green: 6)
sig <- scores.stat.analysis(cell_groups, traitdata.tuto, trait = "Enrollment.IC",
                            test = "kruskal", pval = 0.05, padj = TRUE)
#> 83 significant feature(s) after Kruskal-Wallis test (adjusted p-value (BH) <= 0.05): Dendrogram_pink_group_1, Dendrogram_pink_group_2, Dendrogram_pink_group_3, Dendrogram_pink_group_4, Dendrogram_pink_group_5, Dendrogram_pink_group_6, Dendrogram_pink_group_7, Dendrogram_pink_group_8, Dendrogram_pink_group_10, Dendrogram_pink_group_11, ...
head(sig$Statistics)
